title: The constant-cover quotient and geometric kernel of the arithmetic fundamental group
statement: Let K be a perfect field and L an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let X₀ be a separated finite-type K-scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and suppose X=X₀×_K L [def-pc-base-change] is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Choose a geometric point s:Spec Ω→X [def-weil-geometric-point] with constants embedding i:L→Ω, and put s₀=s followed by the first projection p:X→X₀. For the finite etale fibre functors [def-galois-fibre-functor], there is a continuous surjective homomorphism r:Aut(F_s₀)→Gal(L/K), with the Krull topology, whose kernel is the image of base change Aut(F_s)→Aut(F_s₀) [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality]. For every finite etale K-algebra A [def-galois-categories], K-algebra homomorphism tau:A→L, and z in the fibre of the constant cover X₀×_K Spec A labelled by i∘tau, the point g(z) is labelled by i∘r(g)∘tau. This is the arithmetic exact sequence without the separate injectivity assertion for the geometric map.

proof.text: For a finite intermediate field $E$, the map $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is finite: its algebra is the finite-dimensional $K$-vector space $E$, hence a finite module. It is etale because $K$ is perfect. Finiteness and etaleness survive base change, so $Y_E\to Y_0$ is finite etale. The one-point map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ is surjective; its base change $Y\to Y_E$ is therefore surjective. A separation of $Y_E$ into two nonempty clopens would pull back to a separation of the connected $Y$. Thus every $Y_E$, including $Y_0$, is connected. Their basepoints are the composites of $\bar y$.

source.place: Tag 0BTX, lemma-ses-field, first proof paragraph; Tag 0BNE, finite constant covers

proof.text: Construct the quotient map with its precise convention. For a finite Galois intermediate field $N/K$, identify the fibre of $Y_N\to Y_0$ with $\operatorname{Gal}(N/K)$ using $i$. A natural automorphism $u\in G$ commutes with the deck maps, which act on embeddings by right composition. Consequently its permutation is left multiplication by $u_N(1)$: $u_N(\tau)=u_N(1)\tau$. Naturality for projections $Y_{N'}\to Y_N$ makes these left multipliers compatible under restriction. Since $L/K$ is algebraic, normal (minimal polynomials split in the algebraic closure) and separable (perfectness), [lem-exc-galois-krull-finite-limit] gives a unique $r(u)\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$ with these restrictions. Every finite $E$ is contained in a finite Galois $N$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-set-in-finite-galois-subextension], applied to a finite $K$-basis of $E$. Every embedding $E\to L$ is the restriction of an element of $\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$ by the transitivity clause of [lem-exc-etale-field-galois-classification]. Naturality for the maps of constant covers induced by these embeddings gives $u_E(\tau)=r(u)\circ\tau$ for all $E,\tau$. Composition of these permutations proves that $r$ is a homomorphism. Its finite-coordinate maps are continuous evaluations on finite fibres, hence $r$ is continuous for the specified inverse-limit topology. This also identifies it with the map of structure morphisms: restriction of an automorphism of $F_0$ to the constant covers is exactly that construction. For a finite etale K-algebra A and an embedding tau:A→L, its image is a finite intermediate field E of L/K. Naturality for the induced morphism of constant covers Y_E→Y_A extends the formula to tau. Thus it holds for the general finite etale algebra in the Lean statement.

source.place: Tag 0BNE, lemma-fundamental-group-Galois-group, and Remark 0BQ9, remark-variance; finite-cover construction of the structure homomorphism

proof.text: For each finite Galois $N/K$, the connected cover $Y_N$ is a connected object of the finite etale Galois category, by [lem-galois-finite-etale-connected-object] and [lem-fet-galois-category]. Its fibre is therefore a transitive $G$-set by [lem-galois-transitive]. In the left-translation description of step 2, this says $r_N:G\to\operatorname{Gal}(N/K)$ is surjective. Fix $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$. The closed subsets $C_N=\{u:r_N(u)=\sigma|_N\}$ of the compact group $G$ are nonempty. Any finite collection contains the nonempty $C_M$ for a common finite Galois overfield $M$. Thus their intersection is nonempty: otherwise their open complements would cover $G$, and a finite subcover would contradict this finite-intersection property. Any element in the intersection maps to $\sigma$. This proves surjectivity without choosing a compatible family of arbitrary lifts. Compactness here follows from the profiniteness of the fibre-functor automorphism group [lem-galois-aut-profinite].

source.place: Tag 0BTX, lemma-ses-field, surjectivity paragraph; Tag 0BN3, lemma-tame, applied to each constant cover

proof.text: For each finite intermediate $E$, [thm-galois-fundamental] identifies $\pi_1(Y_E,\bar y_E)$ injectively with the stabilizer $H_E$ of the point $i|_E$ in $F_0(Y_E)$. By step 2, $H_E=\{u\in G:r(u)|_E=\operatorname{id}_E\}$. Under these embeddings, every transition map for $E\subseteq E'$ is the inclusion $H_{E'}\subseteq H_E$: both composites to $G$ act identically on every pulled-back finite cover, by [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality]. Apply [lem-wf-pi1-algebraic-field-limit] with the connectedness proved in step 1. A compatible family in these subgroups is exactly a single element of $\bigcap_E H_E$; its coordinate at $E=K$ is that element. Therefore $j:P\to G$ is injective with image $\bigcap_E H_E=\ker r$. The map $j$ is continuous by functoriality, and is a topological identification with its image by [lem-weil-pbc-compact-hausdorff-bijection], since its domain is compact and its image is a subspace of the Hausdorff group $G$. Together with step 3 this gives the asserted exact sequence of profinite groups.

lean.statement:
theorem arithmetic_exactSequence
    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [PerfectField K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    [IsAlgClosure K L] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic K L]
    (X₀ : Over (Spec (.of K))) [IsSeparated X₀.hom]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType X₀.hom] [QuasiCompact X₀.hom]
    [ConnectedSpace (fieldExtensionBase X₀ L)]
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] [Algebra K Ω]
    (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ fieldExtensionBase X₀ L)
    (i : L →ₐ[K] Ω)
    (hi : s ≫ Limits.pullback.snd X₀.hom
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom i.toRingHom)) :
    ∃ r : Aut (fiber (s ≫ Limits.pullback.fst X₀.hom
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))))) →* (L ≃ₐ[K] L),
      Continuous r ∧ Function.Surjective r ∧
      Set.range (fiberAutBaseChange (Limits.pullback.fst X₀.hom
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))) s) = {g | r g = 1} ∧
      ∀ (g : Aut (fiber (s ≫ Limits.pullback.fst X₀.hom
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))))))
        (A : FiniteEtaleAlgebra K) (τ : A.1 →ₐ[K] L)
        (z : (fiber (s ≫ Limits.pullback.fst X₀.hom
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))))).obj (constantCover X₀.hom A)),
        (fiberConstantCoverEquiv X₀.hom _ A z).1 = i.toRingHom.comp τ.toRingHom →
        (fiberConstantCoverEquiv X₀.hom _ A (g.hom.app _ z)).1 =
          i.toRingHom.comp ((r g).toRingHom.comp τ.toRingHom)
